FOLLOW THE EVIDENCE

The studies.

Full reports and reproducible evidence in the research repository.

Maia score reliability — 27 October 2026

The expected-score percentage was useful as a broad guide to human results in 500 normal-ending games near 1600 and 500 near 2600, with all time forfeits excluded. Exact position-to-position estimates were less dependable: on the same 100 positions, disagreements above 10 percentage points occurred in 9 cases at 1600 and 15 at 2600.

Read the report · Evidence and reproduction guide

Opening variety and Top-P 0.95 — 18 October 2026

The 79M comparison covers 3,000 full games, 5,400 opening rollouts and 180 quality positions at rating inputs 600, 1600 and 2400. Top-P 0.95 with full sampling through the first five moves improves the primary match score and preserves the measured broad opening mix.

Read the report · Evidence and reproduction guide

Temperature and Top-P sampling

Lower sampling settings made Maia stronger in the tested matches but reduced opening variety. The report covers the original 1.0/1.0, 0.5/0.9 and greedy comparisons, plus the 1.0/0.95 follow-up.

Read the report · Evidence and reproduction guide

Move-history input — 9 October 2026

History improved average human-move prediction but strongly reinforced copying in a low-Elo Stonewall test. The recommendation is to keep history off by default; an experimental opt-in setting is proposed separately.

Read the report · Evidence and reproduction guide

Findings, with their limits.

These are independent Mobile Maia experiments, not official Maia-team publications. Results describe the tested models, positions and match conditions. Stronger play does not by itself establish more human-like choices, and selected rating inputs are not calibrated competitive Elo ratings.

Research proposals and released app behavior are separate. See the Stable release notes and experimental Preview channel for implementation status.
